$comment: Libraries whose provenance cannot currently be verified against an in-repo builder.
Every entry is a debt, not a decision: `reason` says why the guard in
nucl_parquet/builder_stamp.py cannot check this library, and `issue` names the
issue that removes the entry. The ledger is self-cleaning — once a library
passes on its own, tests/test_builder_staleness.py fails on the leftover entry
Accepted reasons (the guard rejects anything else):
unstamped        built before manifest.json carried a builder stamp; the next
re-ingest writes one and the entry goes away
external-builder catalog.json declares `"builder": null` — produced by a
pipeline that is not in this repository, so there is nothing
stale-accepted   the builder has changed and we are knowingly shipping
pre-change data; must name the issue that re-ingests it
A `reason` only covers the finding it names. An `unstamped` entry does not
start covering a `stale` finding once the library is finally stamped —
widening an exemption is an edit someone has to make on purpose.

tendl-2023-iso.note: Staged into the repo by a root-level build.py --import-xs (deleted in e84ba665), which copied parquets that had already been produced elsewhere rather than producing them — the ENDF conversion for this library has always been external. The bulk of the library still comes from that import, so there is nothing in the tree to stamp it against. scripts/backfill_xs_nuclides.py landed with #339 but only patches seven target nuclides into an already-imported tree; a stamp naming it would claim provenance over 8.08 M rows it did not produce, which is worse than no stamp. See catalog.json::provenance for the evidence. The entry clears when #346 gives the library a real in-repo builder.
